text:
[Page 1]
   
 
Page 1 of 18 
SCHEDULE 2 – THE SERVICES  
A. Service Specifications 
INTEGRATED SOCIAL CARE DELIVERED TO PATIENTS IN HMP WINCHESTER  
 
1. Background Aims and Objectives. 
BACKGROUND  
The population profile of the prisons has changed rapidly in recent years and there are now  a greater proportion of 
prisoners who are over 50, with the expectation for this to continue to increase significantly over the next 5- 10 years. 
Older prisoners not only bring with them an increased burden of health conditions through age, such as heart disease, 
dementia and diabetes, but also that their physical presentation is at least a decade above their chronological age i 
caused by poor diet, poverty, substance dependencies and lifestyles including homelessness and long-term 
unemployment. The needs of the persons are not neatly divided into either health or social care needs and there are 
significant overlaps and co-
dependencies. Deficiencies in the provision of social care leads to consequent 
deteriorations in overall patient health and raised demand for health care interventions, increasing the burden on 
providers, especially where Persons become too ill to remain in the prisons.   
Throughout this document the term “person” refers to an prisoner within HMP Winchester with either care and support 
needs under the Care Act 2014 or health care needs (patient) or both as applicable. 
Local Authority and NHS E ngland Commissioners recognise the challenges associated with supplying services to 
people within prisons who may have varying levels of complexity and intensity of health and social care needs. The 
provider will understand those challenges and will ensure that the service provides an integrated health and social 
care delivery across all delivery partners. It is the Service Provider’s responsibility to ensure they have a competent 
workforce able to deliver an integrated health and social care service and they must ensure that if the Service provider 
makes any subcontracting arrangements, those subcontractors support the aims and outcomes and standards 
described in this specification. Quality assurance must underpin all service provision.  
The Commissioners want to secure personalised, high quality care and support from a fully integrated health and social 
care service, delivered when the person needs it and in a way that works for them. 
Integration within, and between, care services is especially important when it comes to service provision for people 
over 50 within the prisons. People  in that age category now tend to be developing chronic illnesses and begin being 
subject to multi-morbidity which results in a broad spectrum of needs that have to be met over a long period of time
ii. 
To fulfil this requirement in the community there are a number of possibilities to choose from: health and social care  
services, community and voluntary sector services , domiciliary services as opposed to residential, hospital or clinic 
based services and many more iii iv. However, in prisons the regime imposes conditions and constraints that severely 
limit that choice. Staff and providers must undergo significant vetting procedures, and both equipment and access can 
be limited by security concerns.   
Evidence suggests that joint commissioning between health and social care that results in a multi-component approach 
is likely to achieve better results than those that rely on a single or limited set of strategiesv  
Some of the key componentsvi  are: 
1. a move to community-based multi-professional teams, that include generalists working alongside specialists 
2. a focus on promoting independence, case management and support to home-based care 
3. joint care planning and co-ordinated assessments of care needs 
4. personalised health care plans and programmes  
5. clinical records that are shared across the multi-professional team 
The Service Provider will work in partnership with provider partners including:  
• Hampshire County Council 

[Page 2]
   
 
Page 2 of 18 
• NHS provider services across Hampshire, Southampton City, Portsmouth City and other neighbouring 
authorities.  
• Buddy System 
• HMPPS, and  
• Governors of each establishment to implement social care in the prison environment. 
The services will be provided into HMP Winchester. 
The provider will ensure that the service provides integrated health and social care delivery across all delivery partners 
including Hampshire County Council, NHS provider services, Buddy System , Probation, National Offender 
Management Service (NOMS) and HMP Winchester to implement social care in the prison environment.  
SERVICE AIMS  
1. The Service Provider will support the person to maximise their potential for independence in relation their 
eligible personal care and health needs and work in partnership with the prison service to ensure that The 
persons wider social and welfare needs are supported.  
2. The Service Provider will provide effective, safe and good quality services, delivered in a respectful and 
compassionate manner, and where the person feels secure and confident in the care and support provided 
to them. 
3. The Service Provider will provide personalised care and support delivered when it is needed. The person 
should be at the centre of decisions about how they are cared for and their Care Plan should be designed 
with them and should enhance what they can do for themselves.  
4. The Service Provider will deliver sustainable and sufficient capacity to meet the eligible needs of the person 
within HMP Winchester; characterised by reliability and quality.  
5. The Service Provider will deliver an integrated health and social care service through close partnership 
working with other key stakeholders in particular the prison service and the Buddy System based on mutual 
respect and accountability. 
6. Provide care and treatment which is consistent with national standards (e.g. Quality and Outcomes 
Framework (QOF), NICE guidelines) 
7. The Provider must be registered with the Care Quality Commission (CQC) and provide good or excellent 
quality services as determined by CQC regulations and by the Commissioners 
8. Develop positive and effective interfaces between healthcare services, the wider establishment and the 
local community.  
9. Have the capacity and capability to respond to changes in the health and social care needs of the prison 
population arising from changes in policy.  
 
KEY OBJECTIVES  
1. Efficient use of existing resources by avoiding duplication and ensuring people receive the right care, in the 
right place, at the right time.  
2. Improved experience of health and social care services with better outcomes for people. 
3. To provide a safe environment for all staff, prisoners and visitors. 
4. To maintain the privacy and dignity of all prisoners wherever possible. 
5. To work in partnership with the prison service and the buddy’s to provide a therapeutic environment. 
6. To ensure the person is supported to maximise their independence and reduce reliance on statutorily 
funded support.  
Core Standards 
• Provision of high-quality integrated care services around the needs of the person.  
• All health and social care will be given in the least secure conditions compatible with treatment/care being 
administered. 
• To provide an integrated health and social care service that is focussed on promoting independence and 
supporting patients on Health Care wherever possible to return to the main prison population and by 
proactively managing the throughput of the persons on Health Care and ensuring discharge plans are in 
place. 
• To ensure care plans have clearly stated reablement/recovery goals for each the person.  
• To observe and respect the rights of the person as an individual who has health and social care needs. 
• A highly professional working relationship between health, social care, prison staff and volunteers should 
be evident. 

[Page 3]
   
 
Page 3 of 18 
• Evidence of a prevention approach is adopted in relation to wider social needs utilising the person’s 
personal social networks and volunteers before use of paid staff.   
2a. Service Outcomes   
The service will focus on supporting the individual to achieve the following outcomes: 
• I am able to regain, improve and maintain my independence  
• I can do most things for myself and I am able to choose what care and support I need even if that presents 
some risks 
• I know what I can do to keep myself healthy 
• My emotional, intellectual, social, mental and physical wellbeing are treated as 
equally important 
• I have prompt access to any necessary treatment and care 
• I am well informed about my health and care needs so I can make good decisions 
• My care is delivered consistently by someone who understands me. 
• All the people involved in my care are talking to one another: I know what to expect and that I will only have 
to tell my story once. 
• I know to whom I should talk when I am unhappy with my care 
• I feel safe. I know that my care is high quality and that it meets my needs. 
• I am treated with dignity, respect and compassion. 
• I know that I won’t be admitted to hospital, or kept in hospital, unless it is absolutely necessary. 
• I have the best quality of life possible within the constraints of prison regime 
2b. Service to be provided 
The service will provide up to 37.5 hours of social care support (predominantly personal care see section 5 below) 
delivered by an Agenda for Change Band 3 Health Care Assistant - as detailed and directed within the Designated 
Hampshire County Council (HCC) officers assessment & care plans for prisoners within HMP Winchester. The care 
will be provided within the most appropriate setting within the prison dependent upon the level of need and 
associated risk assessments and plans. 
3. Promoting Independence Choice and Control  
The Commissioners expect that most people  wish to retain as much independence choice and control as possible.  
The service will support and encourage people to maintain, regain or develop self-care skills. Their Care Plan should 
be designed with them and should enhance what they can do for themselves and should foster independence recovery 
and rehabilitation outcomes. 
The Service Provider must ensure that individuals are consulted and give informed consent on all matters concerning 
their care and how it is delivered to them. The requirements of the Mental Capacity Act should be observed where the 
person is unable to make decisions, particularly where necessary personal care is being refused to the detriment of 
the person’s health.   
The Service Provider is expected to encourage the p erson to make best use of all available support including where 
appropriate from peers, Buddy System and prison officers to improve people’s outcomes and reduce demand for 
statutorily funded services. 
The Service Provider must encourage people  to improve their physical and mental health and wellbeing. This would 
include encouraging good diet and exercise, supporting the p erson to maintain family relationships and to retain 
interests and hobbies. 
The Service Provider must ensure that all workers are aware of the different methods of communicating with people 
who have a sensory disability, or other constraints to their communication, and use them as appropriate.  

[Page 4]
   
 
Page 4 of 18 
The Service Provider will support their workers to respond positively and effectively to the diverse make-up and needs 
of people including all those who have protected characteristics through equality legislation for example black and 
minority ethnic people, deaf British sign language users, other people w hose first language is not English, lesbian, 
gay, bisexual and transgender people. Needs arising from specific ethnic, religious, cultural, gender, sexuality, 
disability or age requirements will be identified in the person’s care plan and the service provi der will address those 
needs through their service delivery . Where there is any difficulty in so doing, the Provider should advise the 
Commissioners 
A key component of care and support to people is the monitoring of their health. Any concerns about a person’s health 
or deterioration in the person’s health identified by any of the Service Provider’s staff will be communicated effectively 
and in a timely manner to the responsible medical practitioner to enable appropriate action and interventions to be 
made. 
Appropriate risk assessments must be undertaken by the Service provider in all circumstances where a risk or 
potentially hazardous situation has been identified, ideally before commencement of services under the applicable 
Care Plan or if not at least 48 hours following commencement. The Commissioners must be informed as soon as 
possible of significant or hazardous risks . Risk assessments must take into account that responsible risk taking is a 
normal part of living. Persons must not be discouraged from par ticipating in care activities solely on the grounds that 
here is an element of personal risk, providing they have the mental capacity to understand those risks and where the 
safety of others and in particular the safety of the Provider’s Staff is not threatened. 
4. Safeguarding and Serious Incident Reporting  
  
The Service Provider will ensure that it has in place systems and procedures to safeguard adults and children, as 
defined by the Care Act 2014 and its Statutory Guidance (Chapter 14) and Hampshire County Council Safeguarding 
Adults Multi Agency Policy and Procedures, and Safeguarding Children Policy and procedures. 
The Service Provider must ensure that all its’ Staff receive training in Safeguarding and are compliant with its own 
Safeguarding and Whistleblowing Policy and Procedures and any other policies relating to the mistreatment of adults 
that may be developed. 
In the event that a safeguarding concern is raised by a member of the providers staff team, the prison governor should 
be alerted at the same time as the concern is raised with Adults’ Health and Care via the HCC Designated Officers. 
HCC Officers can provide advice and support with safeguarding investigations. 
The Service Provider will ensure compliance with safeguarding alerts and investigations in line with the services 
procedures and reporting systems (Datix) ensuring that vulnerable prisoners are safeguarded from abuse and neglect. 
Where the safeguarding alert relates to an incident or activity taking place within the prison, it should be raised through 
the Safer Custody routes.  
Where an incident has taken place involving a prisoner that is receiving social care support commissioned by HCC, 
the HCC Officers at the Prison must be informed at the earliest opportunity and be provided with the incident recording 
from Datix.  
The lead prison governor attends the Hampshire County Council Adults Safeguarding Board on behalf of Hampshire 
governors and reports back into the prisons. 
Vulnerable prisoners who may be at risk of safeguarding concerns should be routinely discussed in appropriate forums 
which includes the Complex Care Meeting, Safer Custody and Daily Handover meetings, in order to ensure all staff 
involved in their care and support are aware of the mitigating actions in place to prevent such incidents occurring. 
The process to be followed in the event that a safeguarding concern is raised is contained within the 4LSAB Multi -
Agency Safeguarding Adults Policy & Guidance which can be found here: 

[Page 5]
   
 
Page 5 of 18 
http://www.hampshiresab.org.uk/professionals-
area/hampshire_4lsab_multiagency_safeguarding_adults_policy_guidance/ 
The Service Provider will ensure that all its Staff are aware of, and comply with, the Mental Capacity Act 2005 and the 
Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards (DoLS) including the changes included within the Mental Capacity Amendment Act 
2019 which replaces DoLS with Liberty Protection Safeguards (LPS) from 1
st October 2020. 
The Provider is required to fully cooperate with any Section 42 Safeguarding Adult Enquiries that are raised with the 
local authority, that relates to their Service (or any Sub-Contractors). This can include attendance at Section 42 enquiry 
meetings or any subsequent Section 42 review meetings. 
In the event of an accident causing injury and or medical treatment or serious incident involving either the p erson or 
Care Worker during Service provision, details shall be recorded in the Provider’s incident records and the 
Commissioners shall be informed immediately 
5. Service Description  
The Services to be provided include the areas listed in Schedule 1 of the Health and Social Care Act 2008 
(Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014. Personal Care can include assistance which requires a degree of close 
personal and physical contact with a Prisoner, regardless of age, who, for reasons associated with disability, frailty, 
illness or personal physical capacity is unable to provide it themselves without assistance including, but are not 
limited to: 
Physical assistance given to a person in connection with 
• eating or drinking 
• toileting 
• washing or bathing,  
• dressing, 
• oral care,  
• care of skin, hair and nails (with the exception of nail care provided by a person registered with the Health 
and Care Professions Council as a chiropodist or podiatrist pursuant to article 5 of the 2001 Order), or 
• Prompting to take medication 
The Provider will provide the services via a multi-professional health and social care team focused on the delivery of 
a joint health and social care service plan in conjunction with the prison service that are responsible for supporting the 
wider social and welfare needs of the individual . This will be inclusive of any patients eligible for Continuing Health 
Care (CHC). 
The full range of personal care described within this specification is usually delivered in discrete care visits one or more 
times per day as described within the persons care plan. On occasion usually through a combination of significant 
unpredictable health and social care needs a care worker may need to be on site for a longer period of time to provide 
all commissioned care and support when it is required.  
The timing of social care visits will be at the discretion of the Service Provider unless otherwise clearly stated in the 
care plan i.e. for the coordination of health and social care provision or specific timing of medication support, however 
in all circumstances the service provider will ensure that care visits are timed so that they are responsive to the 
presenting needs and sensitive to the dignity of the person.  
The Service Provider will coordinate the delivery of social care alongside the provision of health services they are 
responsible for to ensure a well -coordinated and integrated health and social care service is delivered to the person  
and that all (health and social care) staffing resources are efficiently utilised to maximise available capacity.  
Assistance with personal care  

[Page 6]
   
 
Page 6 of 18 
The Service Provider must ensure that all such help is given in the least intrusive and discreet, dignified and safe 
manner and the utilization of moving and handling equipment to better manage transfers and care delivery should be 
considered where appropriate (see moving and handling below). 
The Service Provider must be aware of the possibility of cross infection when assisting with matters of personal hygiene 
and must be able to demonstrate it has effective infection control policies and procedures to prevent the spread of 
infectious diseases and that all workers are adequately trained and comply with that procedure. In the event of a 
Worker becoming aware of, or strongly suspicious that, the person has contracted an infectious disease he/she must 
inform their line manager who must then inform the Commissioners. 
Where the Service Provider is concerned about the food and fluid intake of the person or otherwise believes the person 
to be nutritionally at risk they should contact the responsible medical officer or nurse as soon as practicable to ensure 
needs are reviewed, if necessary by a dietary professional. 
When an emergency situation is identified by the Service Provider’s worker, it is expected that sufficient and 
appropriate action will be taken to ensure the immediate health, safety and comfort of the p erson prior to their being 
left alone in accordance with the Service Provider's policies and procedures. 
Assistance with Continence 
The Service Provider will adopt appropriate approaches to restore continence by supporting the management plan 
identified by the suitably qualified nurse. 
When offering assistance with continence the Service Provider must ensure that all workers wear personal protective 
equipment at all times and that toilet facilities are left clean and hygienic after use, with workers always following 
infection control procedures. 
Assistance with continence may also include emptying and changing catheter and colostomy bags, changing 
continence pads and soiled bed linen as required. 
The Service Provider will be expected to report any changes in the person’s urinary and faecal continence and in such 
circumstances further continence advice may be necessary. 
Continence products prescribed by NHS should be used in accordance with the person’s nurse led management plan. 
Where necessary, the Person should be assisted with the correct method of use of continence aids, and with their safe 
and hygienic disposal. 
The Service Provider must ensure that people who experience incontinence and/or  faecal smearing are offered 
assistance with washing and changing into clean dry clothing as soon as practicable.  
Moving and handling requirements 
Where a potential need for equipment is identified by the Service Provider and the equipment is unavailable, or 
where any increase from single handed to double handed care is indicated or where the person refuses to use the 
equipment in circumstances where the Person lacks mental capacity the Service Provider must not rely on a verbal 
referral to the HCC Occupational Therapist who may or may not be on site or message them via NHS IT system that 
HCC staff do not have access to, but rather the service provider should request a social care assessment for the 
allocated HCC practitioners to carry out the required assessments through the agreed referral pathway by emailing 
hcc.ashmpw@nhs.net 
The HCC practitioner will ensure that any necessary equipment identified through a risk assessment is supplied for 
the use of the identified person as soon as possible. In the first instance and if appropriate for the individual equipment 
retained within the prison will be utilised, if that does not suffice, then equipment will be ordered and can if necessary 
be delivered within 24 hours.  
Profiling beds and mattresses can where appropriate be ordered on prescription the designated HCC practitioner can 
advise the service provider accordingly   
All equipment ordered by the commissioners remains the possession of the commissioners and should be returned if 
no longer required by the individual. 

[Page 7]
   
 
Page 7 of 18 
The Service Provider is required to ensure that they have available a nominated person who has the appropriate skills 
and training to complete their own moving and handling risk assessments  and to advise staff providing care on safe 
moving and handling approach to be adopted until moving and handling equipment is available taking into account any 
advice from the designated HCC practitioner. 
The nominated person must be able to identify the need for  and instruct workers in the use of standard moving and 
handling equipment to better manage transfers and care delivery. This would include but is not exclusively limited to 
mechanical or electrical lifting equipment (e.g. hoists and bath lifts), handling belts and glide sheets. 
Where equipment use is identified within the Care Plan as being necessary for safe moving and handling, the Service 
Provider must prior to any worker completing any tasks with that Person; 
• ensure that their workers are trained and assessed as competent to use the equipment provided; and 
• complete their own (Providers) risk assessment of the Person and the environment. 
The Service Providers workers must use equipment that is indicated for such use in the Care Plan and in line with any 
current Service Provider risk assessment. It is essential that where more than one worker is required to carry out care, 
that all workers are present to undertake the task. 
Assistance with medication 
The Service Provider shall be responsible for agreeing the level of support required with reference to the Care Plan 
and must ensure that workers who are required to assist people  to take prescribed medication receive appropriate 
training and work to the Service Providers’ medicines policy.  
The overall aim of the Service Provider’s policy should be to promote independence through encouraging people to 
manage their own medications as far as they are able. 
Assistance with medication must be delivered in accordance with the prescriber’s directions (The Medicines Act 1968) 
and as specified in the Care Plan as  
• General support- this is given when the person takes responsibility for their own medication. Support might 
include opening medicine bottles or an occasional or irregular reminder/prompt to take medication. (level 1) 
• Administering Medication in accordance with the Medicines Administrations Record (MAR), for example 
selecting and preparing medicines for immediate administration by mouth (oral preparations) or medications 
applied externally to the skin and regular and routine reminders to take medications (level 2)  
• Administering medication by specialised techniques for example PEG tubes, suppositories, but only where the 
designated worker has been suitably trained by an appropriately qualified health care professional to administer 
to a named patient. See delegated tasks below. A MAR chart should be used. (level 3)  
 
Delegated Tasks - Delegation by a registered practitioner is the process by which the registered practitioner 
allocates clinical or nonclinical treatment or care to a competent person (the designated care worker) and may 
include for example 
• Administration of particular medications either orally or intravenously  
• Stoma care  
• Catheter and bowel management  
 
The NHS commissioned registered practitioner will remain responsible for the oversight of the care, and accountable 
for the decision to delegate and the service provider is accountable for accepting the delegated task, as well as 
being responsible for the decisions and actions of the delegate (the service provider’s designated worker) in carrying 
it out the task.   
 

[Page 8]
   
 
Page 8 of 18 
The service provider should ensure it retains as a minimum records of the decision of NHS commissioned registered 
practitioner to delegate, the nature of tasks to be delegated and the training and/or supervision provided to the 
worker designated to undertake that task.  
Consent to administer medication should be obtained from the person in writing. The Service Provider will have in 
place policies and procedures in the event that a person is not able to consent or appears not to have the capacity to 
give informed consent. Where consent is refused, medication must not be administered however the Service Provider 
will seek immediate appropriate advice from the prescriber. 
Where the Service Provider is  administering medication,  it will maintain an accurate and up to date Medication 
Administration Record (MAR) chart  
The Service Provider will ensure that Care Workers do not administer any type of non- prescribed or other over the 
counter medication. 
 
End of Life care 
The Service Provider will work towards the End of Life Five new Priorities for Care which are (see 
https://www.england.nhs.uk/ourwork/qual-clin-lead/lac/) 
 
Where end of life care is appropriate the Service Provider will have direct discussions with West Hampshire Clinical 
Commissioning Group (CCG) Continuing Health Care (CHC) team regarding a fast track application for CHC 
funding. The CHC team’s contact details are available via this link: 
 
https://www.westhampshireccg.nhs.uk/nhs-continuing-healthcare 
 
The Service Provider will demonstrate awareness of, and collaborative working towards, local End of Life Care 
systems and protocols, such as the use of EPaCCS (electronic palliative care coordination system), Treatment 
Escalation Plan, Just In Case medication, Advance Care Planning, Gold Standard Framework/General Practice 
palliative care register. 
 
6. Individual Service Arrangements/Service Pathway 
Prisoners will have a range of needs dependent upon their vulnerability, health or disability but could include (this is 
not an exhaustive list): 
• Older people including older people with mental health difficulties (for example dementia); 
• People (under 65 years old) with mental health difficulties; 
• People with a learning disability; 
• People with autism; 
• People with an acquired brain injury or neurological condition; 
• People with a physical and/or sensory disability; 
• People with health needs including long term conditions and continuing health care needs; 
• People at the end of life 
 
Eligibility For Social Care Support (consistent with The Care and Support (Eligibility Criteria) Regulations 2014)  
Any person who is aged 18 and above whose social care needs arise from or are related to a physical or mental 
impairment or illness and as a result of those needs they are unable to achieve two or more specified outcomes 
(see below) and there is, or is likely to be, a significant impact on their wellbeing. This includes people eligible for 
continuing health care. 
 
The specified outcomes are:  
 

[Page 9]
   
 
Page 9 of 18 
a. Managing and maintaining nutrition;  
b. Maintaining personal hygiene;  
c. Managing toilet needs;  
d. Being appropriately clothed;  
e. Being able to make use of their accommodation safely;  
 
A person is to be regarded as being unable to achieve an outcome if he or she is:  
• unable to achieve the outcome without assistance;  
• able to achieve it without assistance, but doing so causes the adult significant pain, distress or anxiety;  
• able to achieve the outcome without assistance, but doing so endangers or is likely to endanger the health 
or safety of the adult, or of others;  
• able to achieve it without assistance but this takes significantly longer than would normally be expected.  
 
Eligibility will be determined by the Hampshire County Council designated officers who undertakes the Care Act 
assessment. A copy of the Care Act assessment and care plan will be shared with the provider as the basis for the 
provider social care delivery plan. 
 
Eligibility for Continuing Health Care 
 
‘NHS continuing healthcare’ (CHC): 'a package of ongoing care that is arranged and funded solely by the NHS where 
the individual has been found to have a 'primary health need' (PHN). ‘In simple terms an individual has a primary health 
need if, having taken account of all their needs (following completion of the Decision Support Tool), it can be said that 
the main aspects or majority part of the care they require is focused on addressing and/or preventing health needs'.  
ADASS and NHS England Guide to the National Framework September 2014 
 
Eligibility for CHC is based on needs, not diagnosis or condition , the care setting, the ability of provider to manage 
care, whether NHS staff are employed to provide care or not, the need for specialist staff, the fact that a need is well 
managed, existence of other NHS funded care, or any other input related rationale. Once an individual referred for full 
assessment West Hampshire CCG coordinates the process on behalf of NHS England.  For patients deemed eligible 
for CHC, the following process is in place:  
For patients deemed eligible for CHC, the following process is in place:  
• Fast Track – forms will be completed by the lead clinician as per standard procedure and submitted to West 
Hampshire CCG for verification.  Care will continue to be provided according to need during the decision-
making process. 
• Non-Fast Track – a joint eligibility assessment is undertaken and then followed by a decision support tool 
process. 
Any social care being supplied to a person will be continued whilst the CHC assessment is being completed.  It is 
important to ensure there is sufficient information provided on the CHC forms to allow for decisions to be reached. 
Social Care Pathway (Referral, assessment, care plan and reviews)  
When a person enters prison, whether via court or transfer from another prison, the Service Provider will carry out an 
initial screening.  This will include social care questions agreed with HCC in order to ascertain what if any 
preventative actions have been taken, details of any health interventions that are in place or planned and the 
likelihood of Care Act Eligibility*.  If social care needs are identified a referral must be made to HCC. 
All referrals must come through the designated NHS email address hcc.ashmpw@nhs.net 
*NB- HCC will wish to work with the service provider on the development of the screening tool and referral form for 
social care assessments. 
The prison service will request an assessment from HCC for people they believe may be eligible for social care.  
All assessments of need will be undertaken by HCC designated officers and where appropriate jointly with NHS 
professionals involved in the person’s care. Where eligibility for funded social care support is established then HCC 
will produce a Care Plan which will be sent to the Service Provider as a referral.  
The Service Provider should read the HCC care plan in conjunction with any current health needs assessment 
including continuing health needs assessment in order to develop its own joint health and social care service plan.  All 
Social Care referrals to the Service Provider will be made by HCC designated officers only and only by means of a n 

[Page 10]
   
 
Page 10 of 18 
Assessment & Care Plan. The Commissioners will accept no financial liability for any Referrals accepted by the 
Provider that have not come from a HCC designated officers. 
The designated HCC officers will be stated on the Care Plan.  
The HCC designated officers will ensure that referral information is of sufficient quality and detail to enable a quality 
response by the Provider and shall email or transfer via other secure electronic means all relevant documentation as 
the Care Plan including; 
• the eligible needs identified by the assessment 
• the needs that the authority are going to meet, and how it intends to do so 
• the identified service outcomes  
• information and advice on what can be done to reduce the needs in question, and to prevent, reduce and 
delay the development of needs in the future 
• a description how the needs will be met and by whom 
• any preferences the person may have regarding how the Service is to be delivered 
• a copy of the assessment, subject to the person’s agreement, as required 
• the planned number of care visits and an assessment of the volume of hours required to deliver the 
identified care per week  
• the timing of any care but only where exact timings are required 
• any special requirements that the person has that should be addressed by the Service Provider 
• a clear statement of the person’s agreement with the Service, or the outcome(s)of any Mental Capacity 
Assessment, or risk assessment that has been undertaken. 
If the Service Provider is not satisfied that the Care Plan is adequate, the Service Provider should contact the HCC 
designated officer s immediately to seek further information or clarification. The Service Provider should, before 
delivering care, contact the person to clarify any areas of need, discuss their preferences and wishes and agree details 
of how care will be delivered and is responsible for feeding back to the HCC designated officer s any changes or 
discrepancies from the details in the Care Plan. 
In undertaking its own assessment of person  needs the Service Provider will undertake any necessary risk 
assessments appertaining to the delivery of care to the person and an assessment of any risks to workers from the 
prisoner or other prisoners on site. Such an assessment should be undertaken in partnership with the prison service 
to ensure that such risks are appropriately mitigated, and workers safeguarded.   
The Service Provider will ensure they attend and are represented by a person of sufficient operational seniority at any 
complex care (multidisciplinary) meeting convened by the prison service intended to coordinate service delivery across 
all provider organisation involved in the person’s care.  
The Service Provider will establish (using their own documentation agreed with CQC & the Commissioners) and 
implement a joint health and social care Service Plan for every person, informed by their HCC and NHS assessments 
and Care Plans and ensure an up to date copy of the Service Plan and other clinical records are available to be shared 
across the multidisciplinary team and is available to the person upon request.  
The Service Provider will maximise opportunities for peer care and support.  NOMS is responsible for the peer care 
and support delivered in this way, according to the ‘Adult Social Care’ (PSI 15/2015) and ‘Prisoners assisting other 
Prisoners’ (PSI 17/2015). Access to the Buddy System requires a social care assessment to identify the need for 
non-personal care support and to agree that a ‘Buddy’ is the correct intervention to meet the person’s needs. If the 
Service Provider considers that the use of the buddy service would be appropriate they should contact the HCC 
designated offer or if no social care assessment has been completed request that an assessment and a Buddy 
Support Plan be completed by making a referral to Hampshire County Council via designated email address 
hcc.ashmpw@nhs.net 
Reviews  
The Service Provider will monitor the achievement of, and progress towards, individual outcomes within the agreed 
timescales identified in the Care Plan. The Service Provider will reduce care packages as soon as practicable when 
outcomes have been met and inform the commissioners accordingly within 1 working day.   
The Provider must signal the need for review of the Care Plan to the commissioners within 3 days, where there is any 
significant change to the person’s needs particularly where that might lead to any reduction or increase in care or 

[Page 11]
   
 
Page 11 of 18 
support delivered or where any long-term change is indicated in the way the person would prefer to have their Service 
provided. 
If the Service Provider’s review indicates that there are additional needs, or the intensity of needs have increased the 
Service Provider discuss with the HCC designated officer or in their absence the HCC Mental Health & Substance 
Misuse Social Care Team Manager to seek agreement to increase the level of social care being provided. An electronic 
copy of the service provider’s assessment should be sent to HCC designated officer/team manager. If an increase in 
care is required urgently outside of office hours – the Provider may implement the increased care but must contact the 
HCC designated officer/team manager, the next working day to discuss the increase in care provision and confirm 
retrospective agreement for the increased care provision.  
Scheduled Reviews will be arranged by the HCC designated officer at least within 2 months of the commencement of 
the service under each Care Plan and thereafter annually. Scheduled reviews have a wider scope and therefore may 
address wider needs than those addressed by the service provider.  
Discharge from the service  
The Service Provider will assist in discharge planning once the person has been agreed via the complex care (MDT) 
meeting/ Service Provider Handover meeting to no longer require or be eligible for social care services or where the 
person is to be discharged into a community setting or other prison and the Service Provider will attend any meetings 
that are required to assess and plan for on-going services as necessary. 
 
The Social Care Provider will continue to provide care until the agreed service cessation date. 
7. Workforce and Training 
It is the Service Provider’s responsibility to ensure they have a competent workforce able to deliver an integrated health 
and social care service and they m ust ensure that if the Service P rovider makes any subcontracting arrangements, 
those subcontractors support the aims and outcomes and deliver the performance and quality standards described in 
this specification. Quality assurance must underpin all service provision.  
The Service Provider will have workforce strategy that that secures and develops the necessary workforce to deliver 
the integrated health and social care service specified and complete a training needs assessment (TNA) which is 
reviewed annually and that responds to the Skills For Care National Minimum Data Set (NMDS).  A flexible approach 
to training is expected to ensure that all workers can undertake appropriate health and social care tasks as appropriate 
The Service Provider must demonstrate that they are following safe recruitment practices compliant with relevant 
national guidelines. All staff will undergo all appropriate checks including additional clearances for the Prison setting 
such as the Disclosure and Baring Service (DBS) and Home Office Security Checks and the Service Provider shall 
have due regard for equality and diversity and equal opportunity in relation to staff recruitment. In particular to ensure 
that the Service Provider’s workforce reflects the diversity of the prison community.  
The Service Provider will ensure that their workers  are appropriately trained supervised and supported to deliver the 
requirements of the Service Specification and CQC requirements.  
The Service Provider will ensure that its entire Staff have undertaken induction training and successfully met the 
common induction standards/care certificate within 12 weeks of employment. The Provider shall not utili se a Care 
Worker in the delivery of Personal Care until they have successfully completed a programme of induction and training 
in line with the new care certificate. Staff will not be able to work unsupervised on an activity until they have been 
signed off as competent in that area of work.  
The Service Provider will ensure that all staff have completed in a timely way any requirements arising from the prison 
service’s security protocols.   
The Service Provider shall ensure that all its Staff who have successfully completed common induction standards/care 
certificate have also received training, as a minimum requirement in: 
• Safeguarding of Vulnerable Adults 
• The requirements of Mental Capacity Act 2005 (including the Mental Capacity Amendment Act 2019 changes) 
• The requirements of the Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards  (and their replacement – Liberty Protection 
Safeguards) 

[Page 12]
   
 
Page 12 of 18 
• The administration of medications 
• The safe Moving and Handling of vulnerable persons 
The Service Provider will ensure that all workers have clear lines of accountability and access to appropriate levels of 
supervision and support, including out of office hours 
The Service Provider will ensure that all its workers deliver care in line with the six fundamental values described in 
‘Compassion in Practice NHS/DoH 2012’; Care, Compassion, Commitment, Courage, Competence and 
Communication. 
The Service Provider will ensure that workers have good communication and listening skills and are sensitive and 
flexible when responding to issues relating to needs of Persons, and that they treat all people with respect and dignity, 
irrespective of their race, disability, gender, religion and belief, sexual orientation and age. 
All workers engaged in delivering care and support to people must have a proficient written and spoken use of English 
Language. 
It is the responsibility of the Service Provider to ensure the good conduct of its workers . Any misconduct, dishonesty 
or behaviour, which is detrimental to the welfare or wellbeing of the Person s, will be thoroughly investigated by the 
Service Provider. The Commissioners will be advised immediately of any such investigation and its outcome. 
8. Quality Assurance  
The Service Provider will have in place a quality management system that ensures internal control of quality and 
performance and consistency of practice that meets the requirements of the Service Specification. 
The Service Provider will work positively and proactively with the commissioners Quality Assurance team(s) address 
any issues of poor performance or noncompliance, including developing and implementing an action plan to address 
said noncompliance or poor performance and to monitoring the delivery of the action plan.  
The Commissioners aim to ensure that any provider it contracts with is delivering services to a CQC good or 
outstanding standard.  The Service Provider will notify the Commissioners immediately of any concerns identified by 
CQC to ensure an action plan to address concerns is in place and details of any notices served by any regulatory 
body.  
The Commissioners (HCC & NHS England) will support the Provider to improve quality and implement a robust 
action plan.  
Failure to work cooperatively and in a timely manner to address quality or safeguarding concerns or continued 
Service Provider failure or serious failures (on its part or on the part of Sub-Contractors) may lead to the termination 
of the Contract in exceptional circumstances 
The service provider should take all reasonable steps to ensure consistency of care to the person. This should include 
a named care worker for each person. If sickness or other events prevent the usual workers from attending it is the 
responsibility of the Provider to ensure that they make appropriate replacement arrangements and take all reasonable 
steps to ensure person is advised of the alternative arrangements.  
It is the right of the p erson and their families to have access to an established and acceptable complaint procedure 
including details on how to use the complaints procedure and the process to be followed by the service provider; 
including timeframes.  
The Provider will identify a manager of sufficient seniority to engage with the commissioners regarding concerns of 
quality or performance who will make themselves reasonably available to meet with the commissioners as requested 
by the commissioners. In addition, they will attend scheduled contract management meetings. 
The Service Provider will inform the Commissioners as soon as practicable of any change of the CQC registered 
responsible individual and/or registered manager of their Service and/or the ‘appropriate persons’ status of their 
registered manager(s). 

[Page 13]
   
 
Page 13 of 18 
All managers of the service will be suitably experienced and qualified to effectively run the Social Care element of 
the service.  They will be trained in, as a minimum; 
• Care Planning, Care Management and Care Review skills 
• Delivering Social Care  
• Mental Capacity Act  
• Safeguarding Investigations  
• Safeguarding for Managers 
Subcontracting  
In the event that the Service Provider subcontracts any social care activity commissioned under this arrangement the 
Service Provider must ensure that that the subcontractor is a CQC registered provider wi th a current CQC rating of 
good or outstanding unless expressly agreed by H CC. The Service Provider remains at all times responsible for the 
quality of the service delivered and its quality assurance process will ensure that the quality of any subcontractor’s 
service is monitored to ensure that the service delivered by the subcontractor conforms to all the quality and 
performance requirements expected of the Service Provider under this agreement. The Service Provider will notify 
HCC whenever a subcontracting arrangement is used.   
9. Records Management 
The Service Provider will ensure that the person and their worker understand the purpose to which any personal 
information that is collected and recorded by the Provider will be used, the Provider’s confidentiality policy and the 
rights of people to view their care records 
All interventions will be clearly recorded as an integrated health and social care record and provide copies of records 
in the event of a subject access request being made to the Council (Data Controller). 
Maintenance of the daily logs to evidence that the Care Plan is being delivered and reviewed including the times and 
interventions and observations of each visit* 
* NB - if records are maintained on a secure IT system then the service provider should ensure that designated HCC 
staff have reasonable access to that system  
Data will be stored securely and only shared with relevant parties.  
All records will be maintained in accordance with the Data Protection Act 1998  
Any security breaches involving information provided by the Council must be reported to the Council’s Data 
Protection Officer within 24 hours of being made aware of the breach. 
The Provider is expected to sign up to an Information Sharing Agreement with the council and HMP Winchester to 
ensure information is shared as necessary, in the best interests of the Prisoner. 
The service provider will record in an electronic format a record of care hours delivered to each person and submit 
those in an agreed format to the designated commissioner for budgeting and financial reconciliation purposes.  
10. Policies and Procedures 
The Provider shall have and maintain a robust set of standards and written protocols, to guide day-to-day practices, 
and to maintain safe and effective operation of all Services.  These shall be developed in accordance with the key 
principles of Children & Families Act 2014; the Care Act 2014; the Mental Health Act 2007; Mental Capacity Act 2005 
(and its 2019 Amendment) and be equivalent to the Council’s own standards.  
All Provider staff shall have access to all Policies and Procedures and are bound by contract to comply with these. 
11. The Management of the Service  
The Service Provider will ensure that the service is available as needed and stated in persons care plans at any time 
of day or night every day of the year.  

[Page 14]
   
 
Page 14 of 18 
The Service Provider will ensure there is an operational manager of sufficient seniority available to accept referrals 
and to arrange delivery of Care Plans and to address any concerns regarding the operational delivery of service at all 
times the service is operating. The Service Provider will supply the commissioners with an up to date list of contacts 
and contact details 
In addition, the Service Provider will ensure that there is a designated person of sufficient seniority available on a day 
to day basis to ensure coordinated social care and health delivery. The Service Provider will notify the commissioners 
of the Service Providers designated person for this purpose, when they are available each day and contact details.  
The Service Provider will be expected to manage reasonable fluctuation in demand flexibly within the core volume of 
hours and to ensure sufficient staffing capacity to cope with those fluctuations in demand. 
The service provider is fully responsible for ensuring that they have the capacity to deliver care and support as required 
and described in Care Plans 365 days per year (366 days in a leap year).  If the service Provider is for any reason 
unable to deliver all necessary care they will notify the commissioners immediately.  
Where persons require intensive and/or complex health and social care the Service Provider should consider whether 
a referral for transfer to Health Care should be made particularly where the person requires double handed care and/or 
care at night. Where ongoing care at night is required then that can only be provided within Health Care where a night 
care worker is available (in exceptional circumstances short term night care may be delivered but only by express 
agreement following appropriate risk assessments by the multidisciplinary team including social care practitioners).  
The Service Provider will deploy its workforce in the most flexible and efficient manner  to ensure that the health and 
social care needs of people are appropriately met . Better outcomes are delivered,  and a more efficient service is 
delivered if segmentation of health and social care tasks can be avoided.   
The Service Provider will designate a Contract Manager of suitable seniority (additional to the registered (CQC) 
manager of the service) responsible for the overall operational delivery of the Service and for liaison with the 
Commissioners’ own operational management team(s) and nominated Contract manager. 
Roles and Responsibilities  
It is necessary for Prison, health and social care staff to understand the duties of each other’s role, to avoid any 
conflict of interest.

12. Performance Management 
HCC designated officers will indicate on each care plan the anticipated number of care hours per week for each 
eligible person. The Service Provider will submit to HCC designated officers via an agreed electronic format the 
actual number of care hours delivered per week to each person and the total delivered per week within HMP 
Winchester. These statistics will be provided on a monthly basis to the local HCC Commissioner and on a 3-monthly 
basis to the NHS England lead commissioner. 
The provider will be required to respond to any ad hoc requests for information made by the commissioners. 
The commissioner requires that the provider have robust Data Quality Procedures in place and all information 
provided to the commissioners must comply with Data Protection requirements and all information provided by email 
must be done so via an encrypted email account, sharing only password protected documents. 
13. Contract Monitor and Audit Requirements 
All records must comply with data protection and accessibility requirements. 
Service providers are to self-inspect all quality assurance requirements when delivering services. Details of self-
audits shall be available on request to the council 
14. Review of the Specification 
Arrangements for revision of this specification are: 
• Any necessary changes to the specification will be agreed in writing between all parties. 
• Wherever such changes are contemplated, the commissioners  will endeavour to consult the Provider to 
reach an agreement as to the implementation of these changes through the contract management process.  
• Any changes to the service specification required by the implementation of any Act or Direction of Parliament 
or Good Practice Guidance shall be binding on both parties for the duration of the Agreement. 
15. Contingency, Emergency Planning and Risk Management  
The Service Provider must assess the risks of the service they are providing and develop business continuity plans, 
in conjunction with the commissioners, to reduce and manage the risks. The Service Provider will undertake a 6 
monthly review of business continuity risks & have in place an action plan to mitigate such risks.  
The business continuity plan will address unplanned circumstances significantly affecting Service delivery including 
the temporary suspension or failure of the provider or any of its subcontractors as well as : 
• Disruption of information or communication technology 
• Staffing level issues due to sickness or other absence 
• Adverse weather 
• Prison Disruption

18a. Eligibility 
Prisoners will need to be detained at either HMP & YOI Winchester and have been assessed by Hampshire County 
Council as meeting the Care Act 2014 eligibility regulations as set out in section 5 of this service spec.

HMP & YOI Winchester. Social care support may be provided within any part of the prison establishment.

Definitions 
In these definitions, unless the context otherwise requires, the following expressions sha ll 
have the following meanings: 
• "Bid”. Proposals submitted by Bidders via the e-procurement system are referred to in 
this document as “Bids”. 
• “Bidder” or “Bidders” shall include any person whom this ITT is addressed, and any 
person who proposes to or does submit a Bid for the Services. 
• "Consortium" means an arrangement between two or more economic operators to 
cooperate in bidding and to rely on each other’s financial and/or technical experience 
to submit a Bid and whether or not the ultimate intended contractual structure is a 
corporate joint venture or a prime/material sub-contractor model. 
• “Consortium Member” an economic operator who is bidding as part of a Consortium. 
• “Commissioner” means the contracting authority listed in section A.1 of this document. 
• “Conditions” means the instructions, conditions and terms applicable to this ITT and 
the procurement of the Services generally. 
• “Contract” means an agreement to provide the specified Services subject to the terms 
and conditions of the Contract specified in this ITT. 
• “ITT” means this Invitation to Tender document (including any appendices and related 
documents) which has been issued to Bidders. 
• “ITT stage” means the formal stage of the procurement process under which Bidders 
submit their Bids. 
• “Material Sub-Contractor" means a sub-contractor that the Bidder is relying on in order 
to meet the Commissioner's Selection Criteria and/or a sub-contractor that the Bidder 
proposes will deliver the whole or a substantial or critical part of the Services. 
• “Preferred Bidder” means the Bidder with the highest total weighted score, who is taken 
through to the Preferred Bidder stage, if this stage is used.

A.4.1 The Commissioner will be contracting for the Services using  the latest version of the

C.1.1 The Commissioner is conducting this procurement in accordance with Regulation 11 
of the PSR Regulations . Bidders must pass all “Pass/Fail” questions in the Basic 
Selection Criteria (BSC)  in order for their quality and financial responses to be 
validated. Bidders should refer to the BSC Bidder Guidance Annex 5 for further 
information on the Basic Selection Criteria (BSC). For those Bidders who successfully 
pass the Basic Selection Criteria (BSC)  and any other compliance questions, the 
evaluation of the remai nder of the Bid will be based on a most economically 
advantageous tender approach, therefore both quality and financial elements will be 
taken into account, as detailed below. 
C.1.2 The Commissioner reserves the right to vary the award procedure for any fair, 
transparent and proportionate reason, at its sole discretion. 
 
C2. Outline process 
C.2.1 Evaluation of Bids will comprise the following elements: 
C.2.1.1 Bid compliance review 
C.2.1.2 Basic Selection Criteria (BSC) evaluation 
C.2.1.3 Qualitative and Financial evaluation of Bids 
C.2.1.3.1 Individual assessment by panel members 
C.2.1.3.2 Bid clarifications (if required, and at any point in the process) 
C.2.2 Moderation, Consensus and Scoring 
C.2.3 Clarification meetings (if required) 
C.2.3.1 Final Moderation (if required) 
C.2.3.2 Preferred Bidder phase (if required) 
C.2.4 Award 
 
C3. Bid Compliance 
C.3.1 Bids must meet all compliance requirements in order for quality and financial scoring 
to be validated. The compliance review will check that Bids: 
C.3.1.1 Are submitted by the due date and time; 
C.3.1.2 Contain all declarations completed as required; 
C.3.1.3 Are in the required format for each element and all mandatory attachments are 
provided; 
C.3.1.4 Are within the Commissioner’s stated year on year financial envelope/s, that no 
material caveats or qualifications are present, and that all tabs are completed within 
the given Financial Model Template. 
C.3.2 Where in the opinion of the Commissioner a Bid does not meet the above criteria then 
it may be deemed non-compliant, and the Bidder disqualified from the applicable Lot/s. 
In this event, further evaluation of the Bid for the applicable Lot/s will not be 
undertaken. 
C.3.3 If any Pass/Fail criteria from any part of the ITT are assessed as “Fail” then the Bidder 
will fail the entire ITT and their quality and financial responses will not be assessed.

C.5.1 Where a bidder does not meet all the compliance requirements and/or does not pass

C.6.1 Bid Evaluators will complete an individual evaluation of Bids using the responses 
received. Evaluation by service users may take place in small groups . Where this

Assessments for each establishment – provided as embedded documents within the 
Information Packs

Bidders to request to receive workforce information (see A.18.)

relied on)

Annex 5 – Basic Selection Criteria (BSC) Bidder Guidance 
 
1.1    Basic Selection Criteria (BSC) Background 
The Basic Selection Criteria (BSC) was developed to simplify the provider selection process 
for businesses, in particular smaller firms, across the public sector.  
Provider selection is a key stage in public procurement where information is gathered on and 
assessments made of the prospective bidders' credentials, before considering tenders.  
The BSC asks potential providers to initially ‘self -declare’ their status against the mandatory 
and discretionary exclusion grounds, selection questions, and additional questions which will 
be evaluated in accordance with the criteria provided. 
 
The BSC is structured in three separate parts: 
 
• Part 1 – Your information and the bidding model 
This covers the basic information about the provider, such as the contact 
details, trade memberships, details of parent companies and bidding model. 
These questions are modelled on the Crown Commercial Services (CCS) 
standard Basic Selection Criteria (BSC) template. 
• Part 2 – Exclusion Grounds 
This covers a self-declaration regarding whether any of the exclusion grounds 
apply. These questions are modelled on the Crown Commercial Services 
(CCS) standard Basic Selection Criteria (BSC) template. 
• Part 3 – Basic Selection Criteria & Project Specific Questions 
Basic Selection Criteria Questions - This covers a self -declaration regarding 
whether the company meets the selection criteria in respect of their financial 
standing and technical and professional ability. These questions are based on 
the Crown Commercial Services (CCS) standard Basic Selection Criteria 
(BSC) template. 
Project Specific Questions - This covers project specific questions added by 
the Commissioner. These questions are designed to specifically test elements 
that are important to the services, including minimum standards required to 
deliver the contract. 
 
 Consortium Bidding / Using Sub-Contractors 
If the Bidder is bidding on behalf of a group, for example, a consortium, or intends to use sub-
contractors, Bidders must clearly identify their chosen Consortium Members and material 
subcontractors in their bid and must be able to evidence that each organisation relied upon 
has agreed to be a Bidder Member. 
Members of a Consortium will not be required to have any formal legal character at the 
procurement stage; however, it must be made clear how the  members of the Consortium 
intend to formalise their relationship to become party to the contract.  This may be evidenced 
by the Bidder by a Heads of Terms or letter of intent between the bidding parties.   
Where the group is proposing to create a separate legal entity, such as a Special Purpose 
Vehicle (SPV) or consortium, they should provide details of the actual or proposed percentage 
shareholding of the constituent members within the new legal entity. They should also provide 
the name for the new entity, and details of its legal and operational structure. An SPV is a legal 
entity that is formed to perform a specific contract. 

[Page 41]
 
41 
There are different actions required for completion of Part 3 of the BSC compared to Part 2. 
• Part 2 of the BSC is a self-declaration, made by you (the Bidder), that you do not meet 
any of the grounds for exclusion 1. If there are grounds for exclusion, there is an 
opportunity to explain the background and any measures you have taken to rectify the 
situation (we call this self-cleaning).  
• A completed declaration in Part 2 provides a formal statement that the organisation 
making the declaration has not breached any of the exclusion grounds. 
• Consequently we require all the organisations that you will rely on to meet the 
selection criteria, to provide a completed Part 1 (Your Information section) and 
Part 2 (Exclusion Grounds). An organisation is ‘relied on’ for the purposes of the 
standard selection questions, if the potential provider is relying on the technical and 
professional ability and/or the economic and financial standing of the organisation to 
meet the selection criteria in Part 3. For example, these could be parent companies, 
affiliates, associates, partners, consortia members or sub-contractors. This means that 
where you are joining in a group of organisations, including joint ventures and 
partnerships, each organisation in that group  that is ‘relied on’ must complete one of 
these self-declarations.  
• A separate template for Part 1 and Part 2 in Word format  is provided in the 
document suite in the e -Procurement system for those organisations that are relied 
upon, to complete and be uploaded with your submission.  
• The lead organisation should complete Parts 1 & 2 on behalf of their organisation using 
the main questionnaire. (NB: the responses to question 1.2 must also reflect the 
overarching bidding arrangements). The lead organisation should make it clear who 
the lead member of the group is, and who will be contractually responsible for delivery 
of the Contract.  
• Part 3 - a response to all questions within these sections is required. If you are bidding 
on behalf of a Consortium or you intend to use sub-contractors, you should complete 
all of the BSC within the main questionnaire on behalf of the consortium and/or any 
sub-contractors, providing one composite response and declaration.  
 
The Commissioner recognises that arrangements set out in the BSC in relation to a group of 
economic operators (for example, a consortium) and/or use of sub-contractors, may be subject 
to change and will, therefore, not be finalised until a later date. The Bidder should notify the 
Commissioner immediately of any change in the proposed arrangements, and ensure a 
completed Part 1 and Part 2 is submitted for any new organisation relied on to meet the 
selection criteria. The Commissioner will make a revised assessment of the submission based 
on the updated information.  The Commissioner reserves the right to deselect a Bidder or 
group prior to any award of contract, based on an assessment of the updated information. 
 
 
 
 
1 For the list of exclusions please see: 
https://www.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/551130/List_of_Mandat
ory_and_Discretionary_Exclusions.pdf 

[Page 42]
 
42 
1.2  Self-Cleaning 
A Bidder who has been excluded from public procurement can have the exclusion ended if 
they effectively ‘self-clean’.  If any Bidder has breached any of the exclusion grounds in Part 
2 of the BSC, they should provide sufficient evidence that provides a summary of the 
circumstances and any remedial action that has taken place.   
 
Bidders are required to demonstrate that they have taken remedial action, to the satisfaction 
of the Commissioner in each case. In order for the evidence provided to be sufficient it must, 
as a minimum, prove the supplier has ‘self-cleaned’ as follows: 
 
• paid or undertaken to pay compensation in respect of any damage caused by 
the criminal offence or misconduct; 
• clarified the facts and circumstances in a comprehensive manner by actively 
collaborating with the investigating authorities; and 
• taken concrete, technical, organisational and personnel measures that are 
appropriate to prevent further criminal offences or misconduct. 
 
The measures taken shall be reviewed taking into account the gravity and particular 
circumstances of the criminal offence or misconduct. If such evidence is considered by the 
contracting Commissioner (whose decision will be final) as sufficient, the Bidder  shall be 
allowed to continue in the procurement process. If the Bidder cannot provide evidence of ‘self-
cleaning’ that is acceptable to the Commissioner, they will be excluded from further 
participation in the procurement and provided with a statement of the reasons for that decision. 
 
1.3     Format of BSC Response 
The BSC questions are completed once, regardless of how many lots are applied for.  This is 
unless a bidder is relying on the capacity/capability of different sub -contractors for different 
Lot responses.  
All questions must be completed in full, and in the format requested.  If a question does not 
apply to you, please state ‘N/A’.  
The BSC has been provided as a Requirement section within the online questionnaire, (within 
the e-procurement system). 
There are separate (optional) placeholders which should be used to upload any Part 1 and 
Part 2 declarations, that are required for organisations that are relied upon  and for any 
additional information, (i.e. self -cleansing evidence) which is required in response to any of 
the questions,  and submitted as part of the Bid.  
All electronic files submitted should be clearly named, including the Bidder’s name and the 
question number to which that electronic file relates.   
The Commissioner reserves the right to reject any BSC that is either incomplete or not 
compliant in regard to the required format.  This may lead to a Bidder’s bid being rejected 
without evaluation, and the Bidder’s exclusion from further consideration.  Any such rejection 
will be solely at the Commissioner’s discretion. 
Responses to questions must be self -contained and not rely on information provided in 
response to other questions.  Evaluators will only consider the information provided within 
each response and may not have access to other sections of the bid. 
When evaluating a BSC submission, the Commissioner will only consider information provided 
in a Bidder’s formal response to this BSC, Bidders must not assume that the Commissioner 
has any prior knowledge of the Bidder or Consortium Members or sub-contractors , its practice 
or reputation, or its involvement in existing services, projects or procurements. 

[Page 43]
 
43 
The Bid Return Instructions at section A.12 of this document apply to the BSC.  
 
1.4      Economic and Financial Standing 
 Bidders are required to submit financial information in support of their response to Section 3 
(questions 3.1 / 3.2). Financial information will be assessed in line with the criteria set out at 
section C.11.3 of this ITT document.  
 
1.5      Technical and Professional Ability 
Contract examples may be given from either the public or private sector, and may be provided 
from any organisation ‘relied on’ in the completion of the BSC.  Contract examples must be 
relevant to the requirement and must have been performed during the past three years.  
The Commissioner reserves the right to contact the named contact /s provided by the 
Preferred/successful Bidder prior to award of contract. Such contact will be for due diligence 
purposes, in order to  confirm the accuracy of the information provided and confirm that the 
Preferred/successful Bidder has the necessary human and technical resources and 
experience to deliver the contract. Bidders are  therefore requested to submit details of 
contracts where the named customer contact is prepared to provide written evidence  in line 
with the above.  Bidders may include contracts held with the Commissioners. 
The Commissioner confirms that it will keep confidential, and will not disclose to any third 
parties, any information obtained from a named customer contact, other than to the Cabinet 
Office and/or contracting authorities defined by the regulations, or pursuant to an order of the 
court or demand made by any competent Commissioner or body, where the Commissioner is 
under a legal or regulatory obligation to make such a disclosure and in accordance with its 
obligations under the Freedom of Information Act (FOI A) or Environmental Information 
Regulations (EIR). 
 
1.6    Self-declarations / Self-certification 
As outlined above, Bidders are required to self -declare or self -certify that they meet certain 
criteria contained in the BSC.  
Unless specifically requested in the BSC or otherwise stated, Bidders are not required to 
submit evidence to their responses at this stage (e.g. where a bidder is asked to self -certify 
they have, or will have relevant levels of insurance in place). 
The Commissioner reserves the right at any  point in the procurement , including prior to the 
award stage  to request from any Bidder (and any organisations relied upon to meet the 
selection criteria) to submit evidence. When requested by the Commissioner, the Bidder must 
submit this evidence within the timeframes given.   
If the Bidder fails to provide the required evidence within set timeframes, or the evidence 
proves unsatisfactory, this may result in the corresponding BSC question being scored as a 
‘Fail’ which, at the sole discretion of the Commissioner, will result in the bid being disqualified. 
Where a Preferred Bidder stage is undertaken prior to award, if evidence is requested by the 
Commissioner from the Preferred Bidder during this stage and the Preferred Bidder fails to 
provide the required evidence within the set timeframes, or the evidence  proves 
unsatisfactory, the Commissioner may, at its absolute discretion, disqualify the Bidder from 
the procurement process and consider alternative options in order to ensure continuity of 
services and patient safety. 
 
 

[Page 44]
 
44 
1.7    Consequence of misrepresentation  
If you seriously misrepresent any factual information in filling in the  BSC, and so induce an 
authority to enter into a contract, there may be significant consequences.   
You may be excluded from the procurement procedure, and from bidding for other contracts 
for three years. If a contract has been entered into you may be sued for damages and the 
contract may be rescinded. If fraud, or fraudulent intent, can be prove n, you or your 
responsible officers may be prosecuted and convicted of the offence of fraud by false 
representation, and you must be excluded from further procurements for five years.  
 
1.8    Carbon Reduction Plan 
The commissioner has determined that the Procurement Policy Notice (PPN) 06/21 applies to 
this procurement, and therefore potential bidders are required to submit a Carbon Reduction 
Plan (CRP) which details their organisational carbon footprint and confirms their commitment 
to achieving Net Zero by 2050.  
Carbon Reduction Plans are to be completed by the bidding supplier 2 and must meet the 
reporting requirements set out in supporting Guidance 3, and include the supplier’s current 
carbon footprint and its commitment to reducing emissions to achieve Net Zero emissions by 
2050.  
The CRP should be specific to the bidding entity, or, provided certain criteria are met, may 
cover the bidding entity and its parent organisation. In order to ensure the CRP remains 
relevant, a Carbon Reduction Plan covering the bidding entity and its pare nt organisation is 
only permissible where the detailed requirements of the CRP are met in full, as set out in the 
Technical Standard4 and Guidance, and all of the following criteria are met:  
• The bidding entity is wholly owned by the parent;  
• The commitment to achieving net zero by 2050 for UK operations is set out in the 
CRP for the parent and is supported and adopted by the bidding entity, demonstrated 
by the inclusion in the CRP of a statement that this will apply to the bidding entity;  
• The environmental measures set out are stated to be able to be applied by the 
bidding entity when performing the relevant contract; and  
• The CRP is published on the bidding entity’s website.

Question: We note the that commissioners have set financial envelopes in anticipation of 2027/28 prices and the requirement therefore for bids to be priced in 2027/28 terms. In relation to this can commissioners please confirm the following:

a) That any variation from the assumed net business rules uplifts of 0.73% for 2026/27 and 0% for 2027/28 will be passed on to the contract values.

Commissioner response: a) As indicated, NHS England would not uplift the contract value within the first year of the contract. However, should the final operating framework uplift, once published for 2027-28, be significantly different to our estimated uplift, the Commissioner would look to review the contract value, with a view to incorporate any significant difference within the contract value. Annual uplifts will be incorporated, once finalised and published, for each contract year with the first one commencing on 01st April 2028. Please remember the finance and business rules in the Revenue Finance and Contracting guidance reflect the expected cost pressures facing providers in the next financial year, and, depending on these foreseen pressures, can be positive or negative. Any major variation / deviation from the assumed uplifts, as indicated, will be reviewed and discussed with the providers at the appropriate time.

b) Correct, this should be 1st April 2028. The ITT Bidder Instructions and FMTs have been updated to correct this (please refer to the updated versions referenced in column H). 
As detailed in the FMT – ‘Notes on template completion’ tab (and in the ITT Bidder Instructions at A.6.6), ‘The price at the beginning of each financial year will be subject to the finance and business rules in the NHS Operating Framework, for clarity, this means that the bids will be uprated on the 1st April 2028 and on this day in future years. The finance and business rules in the Operating Framework reflect the expected cost pressures facing providers in the next financial year, and, depending on these foreseen pressures, can be positive or negative.'
For reference, within the relevant tables, the figures in recent years are as indicated, although nothing can be deduced from these to infer future trends.

c) As referenced in the above responses to a and b and within the relevant ITT documentation, the uplift figures in recent years have been provided for the purposes of reference only. The commissioner would like to reiterate that these figures cannot be used to to infer any future trends and any assumptions based on these would remain the responsibility of the bidder.
